title: Sharp determinant bounds for amplified antisymmetric channels and a noise law for noncommutative rank
abstract: We study the largest normalized determinant in a Kraus matrix space after amplification by a completely depolarizing channel. For the three-dimensional antisymmetric channel, we prove a bound uniform in the auxiliary dimension, identify its exact value 2^(2/9)/4, and show that a finite amplification attains it if and only if its dimension is divisible by three. The proof balances a determinant maximizer, fixes its second and fourth singular-value moments, and uses a quadratic majorant of the logarithm. Combined with known unitary constructions, this determines the regularized value for every Holevo-Werner channel: dimension three is the unique exceptional case. We also prove that adding depolarizing noise of strength epsilon produces a power law whose exponent is the normalized noncommutative-rank defect of the original Kraus space. The latter estimate is uniform over all auxiliary dimensions and has a matching lower bound at one fixed finite dimension. These results sharpen finite-dimensional examples and an exact-rank criterion into, respectively, an infinite-amplification optimum and a quantitative noise law. We state the operational interpretation for tests of an unknown global unitary separately from free ancillary assistance.
